business_problem: IBM’s CIO organization needed a digital assistant that could help employees complete routine work faster and search across enterprise knowledge without exposing confidential or sensitive information.
solution_summary: IBM’s CIO organization built AskIBM in 60 days using IBM watsonx.ai and IBM Granite foundation models as a retrieval-augmented employee assistant. The platform was designed to automate everyday knowledge-work tasks such as drafting email, translating documents, summarizing long files and searching for information. Strategic internal IBM content—while excluding confidential, sensitive personal and customer information—was ingested into the system so the assistant could ground responses in approved enterprise knowledge. The initial alpha release started with about 5,000 multilingual documents and expanded to more than 30,000 by July 2024. AskIBM applies RAG to retrieve relevant content and generate tailored answers, while IBM’s legal, privacy, cybersecurity and AI-ethics reviews served as production guardrails. The result is a global internal assistant that puts enterprise knowledge and generative AI directly into employee workflows.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Hosts the generative AI environment used to build and run AskIBM.

solution_components.name: IBM Granite
solution_components.role: Provides the foundation models used to generate grounded responses for employee tasks.

data_flow: Approved internal IBM documents are ingested into AskIBM’s RAG pipeline, retrieved based on employee prompts and used by watsonx.ai and Granite models to generate task-focused responses for knowledge workers around the company.
integration_points: Legal, privacy, cybersecurity and AI ethics reviews
business_outcome: AskIBM put a governed internal assistant in front of IBM employees worldwide, reducing friction in everyday knowledge work and accelerating the company’s own AI adoption journey.
metrics: Over 30,000 documents were ingested into AskIBM
